label: UK advertising agencies on the VAT/PAYE register
statement: The UK had 18,985 advertising agencies (SIC 73.11) on the VAT and/or PAYE business register in 2026, up 8.6% on 17,485 in 2025, according to the ONS.
sample: ONS UK business: activity, size and location, 2026; VAT and/or PAYE based enterprises classified to SIC 73.11, figures rounded to the nearest 5.
caveat: An enterprise count on the VAT/PAYE register, not a Companies House company count and not a count of SEO agencies. SEO and digital agencies can also register under other SIC codes, and businesses below VAT/PAYE thresholds are excluded.

label: UK Google searches ending without a click
statement: 69.5% of UK browser-based Google searches ended without a click in SparkToro's analysis of Similarweb data.
period: January to April 2026 in the shared method; UK period not separately confirmed
sample: Similarweb UK desktop and mobile-web panel; panel size not disclosed.
caveat: Excludes the Google mobile app. The shared method labels its period US. Zero-click activity does not establish satisfaction or isolate AI Overview effects.

label: Open-web clicks per 1,000 UK Google searches
statement: SparkToro estimated 232 clicks to the open web per 1,000 UK Google searches, including both organic and paid results.
period: January to April 2026 in the shared method; UK period not separately confirmed
caveat: This is not 232 organic visits. Multiple-result clicks may be undercounted. Alphabet-owned destinations are excluded from the open-web measure.

label: Google's share of UK search referrals
statement: Google generated 91.35% of UK search-engine referrals in Statcounter's September 2026 all-platform sample.
sample: Search-referred page views on sites with Statcounter measurement.
caveat: Measures clicked referrals, not searches or people. Zero-click activity is absent. September data remain within Statcounter's 45-day revision window.

label: Bing's share of UK desktop search referrals
statement: Bing generated 18.44% of UK desktop search-engine referrals in Statcounter's September 2026 sample, up from 10.37% in August 2026.
sample: Search-referred desktop page views on Statcounter-network sites.
caveat: Publisher mix affects the sample. This is a device-specific referral share, not the share of UK adults using Bing. Statcounter's daily desktop data show the step change from early September 2026; the cause is not stated and the month remains within the 45-day revision window.

label: Bing's share of UK mobile search referrals
statement: Bing generated 0.43% of UK mobile search-engine referrals in Statcounter's September 2026 sample.
sample: Search-referred mobile page views on Statcounter-network sites.
caveat: Compare with the desktop figure only as referral shares. These values do not reveal the device split of all UK searches. Recent data can be revised.

label: Google's share of UK traditional search queries
statement: Google handled more than 90% of UK traditional general-search queries throughout January 2018 to June 2025, according to the CMA.
sample: CMA analysis of traditional general-search providers' query data.
caveat: Exact shares are confidential. This historical query measure is distinct from Statcounter referral shares and does not establish a current share.

label: UK search advertising expenditure
statement: UK search advertising expenditure reached £17.9bn in 2025, representing 44% of digital ad spend in IAB UK's study.
sample: IAB UK / Oliver Wyman revenue submissions, public figures and market modelling.
caveat: Paid search expenditure is not SEO agency revenue. The methodology changed in 2025; use the restated prior-year series for growth comparisons.

label: UK online adults who used search engines
statement: 96% of UK online adults reported using a search engine in the previous year in Ofcom's autumn 2025 survey.
sample: UK online adults aged 16+; 7,029 online respondents in the wider survey.
caveat: Self-reported annual use measures reach, not frequency or query volume. Survey changes limit year-on-year comparisons.

label: Search users selecting only the paid-placement explanation
statement: 52% of UK search-engine users selected only the correct paid-placement explanation in Ofcom's Google results test.
sample: 6,731 search-engine users aged 16+; a walking-boots search example.
caveat: 66% selected the paid-placement answer at all; 52% selected only that answer. This prompted test measures ad recognition, not organic CTR.

label: UK adults reporting AI-tool use
statement: 54% of UK adults reported using AI tools in Ofcom's autumn 2025 survey.
sample: 3,768 UK adults aged 16+ in survey Module 1.
caveat: Includes uses beyond search. Self-reported AI adoption is not an AI-search market share.

label: UK online adults reading AI search summaries
statement: 75% of UK online adults said they read AI-generated search summaries at least sometimes in Ofcom's autumn 2025 survey.
sample: 3,515 online adults aged 16+ in Module 1; prompted with a summary example.
caveat: Reported reading is not the frequency of summaries appearing, a citation rate or a measure of resulting clicks.

label: Conventional-result clicks with and without AI summaries
statement: Pew observed conventional-result clicks after 8% of US Google visits with an AI summary versus 15% without one.
period: Behaviour: March 2025; results captured 7 to 17 April 2025
caveat: Observational groups had different queries. Results were captured after the original searches. The comparison does not isolate a causal AI-summary effect.

label: AI-summary visits producing a source-link click
statement: Only 1% of visits to Google results with an AI summary produced a click on a cited summary link in Pew's US sample.
period: Behaviour: March 2025; results captured 7 to 17 April 2025
sample: 900 US adults; 12,593 observed searches with an AI summary.
caveat: Pew matched the next visited URL against the first three summary sources. A URL appearing in both places was counted as an AI-summary click.

label: Local searchers considering three or fewer businesses
statement: 72% of BrightLocal's active US local-searcher panel considered three or fewer businesses before choosing.
sample: 1,227 US consumers who searched online for a local business within three months.
caveat: Self-reported behaviour from a screened vendor survey. It is neither UK consumer behaviour nor observed Local Pack click-through rate.

label: Sample clicks from rounded position buckets 1 to 10
statement: Rounded position buckets 1 to 10 produced 1,448 of 1,667 clicks in Sunny Patel's portfolio dataset, or 86.9%.
sample: 53 qualifying Search Console properties; returned query rows with at least 50 impressions; bucketed GSC aggregates.
caveat: Calculated from the published aggregates. API extraction caps each property at 5,000 rows without pagination. Property overlap was not verified. Position buckets do not prove that moving a query causes the same gain.

label: Identified AI referral sessions across 104 portfolio sites
statement: Edition 2 of Sunny Patel's AI referral study reports 6,165 AI-matched sessions out of 334,744 total sessions (1.84%) across 104 owned portfolio sites from 24 June to 21 September 2026.
sample: GA4 session-source matching across a 108-property owned portfolio frame, 104 sites with sessions. Replaces edition 1's 12 hand-picked high-AI-traffic sites (4,717 sessions, 28 May to 26 August 2026).
caveat: One owner's portfolio, not a representative sample of websites. No country restriction. Referral sessions do not measure citations, people or incremental sales, and Google AI Overviews or AI Mode clicks cannot be separated from organic search.

label: ChatGPT's share of identified portfolio AI sessions
statement: ChatGPT-matched sources (source containing "chatgpt" or "openai") accounted for 5,350 of the study's 6,165 identified AI referral sessions, or 86.8%.
sample: Same 104-site GA4 owned-portfolio panel (edition 2). Edition 1's 12-site figure was 90.1%.
caveat: A share of identified AI referrals in this portfolio, not AI market share. Source attribution can miss untagged visits. Published totals are not an independent analytics audit.
